
## Errors

Processing can return `409 DUPLICATE_FIELD`, `FIELD_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT`, `DUPLICATE_APPLICATION`, `APPLICATION_FIELD_CONFLICT`, `PROCESSING_CONFLICT`, `FIELD_CHANGED`, or `APPLICATION_CHANGED`. Signed portal setup can return `503 PORTAL_SAS_UNCONFIGURED`. A workflow can also return `422 UNSUPPORTED_APPLICATION_METHOD`; HTTP input validation normally catches this first as `INVALID_REQUEST`. See [assessment issues](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#assessment-issue-codes) for incomplete evidence returned with HTTP 200.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

---

# V2: Submit bulk checks

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/bulk-submit.md

> Submit multiple applications with shared or per-field products and crops

Endpoint: `POST https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/esa-check/bulk`

Submit one job containing 1–100 field applications. Put values shared by your fields at the top of the request. Inside `fields[]`, supply each field's identity and boundary, plus any values that differ for that field.

**A field value replaces the matching top-level value for that field only.** Other fields still use the top-level default. Products and crops follow the same rule: arrays replace the entire array; they never merge.

## Request

### Idempotency-Key

header parameter; string; optional.

Optional, strongly recommended. One to 200 characters. Scoped to your provider/account; reuse it only with identical effective inputs.

### provider_id

body parameter; string; required.

Your assigned provider, matching the key.

### account_id

body parameter; string; required.

Your account identifier.

### provider_group_id

body parameter; string; required.

Required nonempty work-order/job identifier, up to 200 characters. Shared by every field.

### fields

body parameter; object[]; required.

One to 100 field entries. Each requires `application_id`, `field_name`, and `field_boundary`; `provider_field_id` is optional.

### products

body parameter; object[]; optional.

Default products; each field must have effective products.

### crop

body parameter; string[]; optional.

Default crops; each field must have an effective crop array. An explicit empty array is valid.

### pest

body parameter; string[]; optional.

Default pests, unless replaced by the field or product.

### application_date

body parameter; string; optional.

Default `YYYY-MM-DD` application date.

### application_method

body parameter; string; optional.

Default supported method.

### gpa

body parameter; number; optional.

Default positive spray gallons per acre; nullable.

### droplet_size

body parameter; string; optional.

Default supported droplet category/code; nullable.

### boom_height

body parameter; string; optional.

Default `low` or `high`; nullable.

### user_email

body parameter; string; optional.

Default valid email; nullable.

### include_geometry

body parameter; boolean; optional; default: false.

Top-level response option applied to every field.

### include_soil_analysis

body parameter; boolean; optional; default: false.

Top-level response option applied to every field.

### include_mitigations

body parameter; boolean; optional; default: false.

Top-level response option applied to every field.

### buffer_distance_miles

body parameter; number; optional; default: 1.

Top-level PULA search buffer, clamped to 0–10 miles.

## Where each value belongs

| Location | Properties | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Top level only | `provider_id`, `account_id`, `provider_group_id` | Required once; apply to every field. You cannot mix providers, accounts, or groups within one job. |
| Top level only | `include_geometry`, `include_soil_analysis`, `include_mitigations`, `buffer_distance_miles` | Apply to every field. Defaults are `false`, `false`, `false`, and `1`. |
| Inside each field only | `application_id`, `field_name`, `field_boundary` | Required in every field entry. |
| Inside each field only | `provider_field_id` | Optional. Omitted or `null` uses that field's `application_id`. |
| Top level and/or inside a field | `products`, `crop`, `application_date`, `application_method` | Each field needs a value, either inherited or supplied on that field. |
| Top level and/or inside a field | `pest` | Default pests for products without their own `pest` list. |
| Top level and/or inside a field | `gpa`, `droplet_size`, `boom_height`, `user_email` | Optional. A field can inherit, replace, or explicitly clear a default with `null`. |

You may omit all shared application settings and specify them separately in every field. You may also mix shared defaults and overrides in the same request. See [single-check inputs](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/esa-check) for allowed methods, droplet sizes, product properties, and field boundary limits.

## How defaults and overrides resolve

For each field, the API starts with the top-level defaults, replaces each property explicitly supplied by that field, then validates the resulting application independently.

| What you send inside a field | Effective value for that field |
|---|---|
| Omit `products` | Use the complete top-level `products` array. |
| Supply `products` | Use only that field's complete product array. Products are not matched or merged by EPA number or array position. |
| Omit `crop` | Use the top-level crop array. |
| Supply `crop: ["Soybeans"]` | Replace every top-level crop with `Soybeans`. |
| Supply `crop: []` | Use an empty crop array; do not inherit. This is valid input. |
| Omit `gpa` | Use the top-level GPA, if present. |
| Supply `gpa: 20` | Use 20 for this field. |
| Supply `gpa: null` | Clear this field's GPA even if the top level specifies one. The same rule applies to droplet size, boom height, and email. |
| Supply `products: []`, `pest: []`, or `crop: null` | Reject the entire submission with `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. |

**To change just one product's rate, send the full desired product array for that field**, including the other products you want retained. Each product needs its required properties (`product_name`, `rate`, and `rate_unit`); a partial product such as `{ "rate": 28 }` is invalid.

### Pest precedence

Pests have one additional level of precedence: **product `pest` → field `pest` → top-level `pest`**. Product pest lists stay attached to their product even when the product array is inherited. A field pest override affects only products without their own pest list. Every product must end up with a nonempty pest list.

### Worked example

The complete cURL request on this page submits two fields using Liberty Ultra with `Broadcast-Ground`:

North supplies no application-setting overrides, so every shared default applies. South supplies a complete replacement product array, replaces `crop` and `gpa`, and clears `boom_height` with `null`. South still inherits the date, method, pests, and droplet size.

| Setting | Shared default and North result | South result |
|---|---|---|
| Products | Liberty Ultra, 32 fl oz/ac | Liberty Ultra, 28 fl oz/ac (replaced) |
| Crop | `Corn` | `Soybeans` (replaced) |
| Pests | `Waterhemp` | `Waterhemp` (inherited) |
| Method | `Broadcast-Ground` | `Broadcast-Ground` (inherited) |
| GPA | `15` | `20` (replaced) |
| Droplet size | `VC` | `VC` (inherited) |
| Boom height | `low` | Unspecified (`null` clears the default) |

Clearing an application setting does not establish that it is irrelevant to compliance. Missing information can leave the assessment `indeterminate`.

## Validation before acceptance

All fields are validated before the API accepts a job. **One invalid field rejects the entire submission with `422 INVALID_REQUEST`; no job is created.** This differs from processing failures after acceptance, where some items can succeed and others fail.

- Unknown top-level and field properties are rejected. For example, `fields[0].include_geometry` is invalid because that option belongs at the top level.
- Supplied defaults must themselves be valid, even if every field overrides them. Omit an unused default instead of sending an invalid placeholder.
- `application_id` values and effective `provider_field_id` values must be unique within the submission.
- Each field boundary may contain at most 5,000 coordinate positions across all its rings. The total request body limit is 5 MB.

For example, a duplicate application ID on the second field returns:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "details": [{
      "code": "custom",
      "path": ["fields", 1, "application_id"],
      "message": "Duplicate application_id in bulk submission"
    }]
  }
}
```

Issue paths use zero-based array indexes, so `fields[1]` is the second field. Correct the indicated input and resubmit. See [validation examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#validation-examples) for missing group IDs, pests, and unknown properties.

## Accepted response and polling

The response is **202 Accepted**, including on an idempotent replay or immediate completion. It includes `Location` (the status path) and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Responses with `status: "queued"` or `"processing"` also include `Retry-After: 5`. Both URLs are relative to `https://esa.acreblitz.com`.

When the returned status is `queued` or `processing`, poll [job status](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/bulk-status) and fetch [results](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/bulk-results). A job with some failed items can finish as `completed_with_errors`. A succeeded item can still contain an indeterminate or unmet compliance assessment.

### Immediate completion when no products require ESA

Before enqueueing a new job, the API collects the unique products used across **all fields**, including inherited top-level products and field-specific replacements, and resolves them together using the existing product cache. Rates, crops, and pests remain specific to each field. A top-level product that every field replaces is unused and does not affect the check.

When every product is resolved and none requires ESA, the job completes in the submission response:

- `status` is `completed` and top-level `esa_required` is `false`.
- `items` contains all per-field results in submission order, using the same item structure as the results endpoint. Each item has `status: "succeeded"`, `attempts: 0`, and `result.compliance.status: "not_applicable"`.
- No processing is queued, and no soil, PULA, or drift calculations or field/application creation occur. Bulk job and result records remain available for the normal 30-day retention period.
- Because no PULA lookup runs, every product's `pulas` is empty and `summary` counts are zero. Jobs that require ESA return each product's PULA limitations in the item `result`; see [bulk results](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/bulk-results).
- You can consume `items` immediately without polling. The status/results URLs remain available, and an identical idempotent replay returns the same stored results.

If any used product requires ESA, is unresolved, or has unknown ESA status, the request follows the queued workflow. A reference lookup failure returns an HTTP error without creating a new job. Unknown products are never treated as confirmed no-ESA products. Validation of every field still happens before acceptance.

Example immediately completed response for a one-field submission:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "job_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "status": "completed",
  "total_items": 1,
  "replayed": false,
  "esa_required": false,
  "status_url": "/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "results_url": "/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001/results",
  "items": [
    {
      "item_index": 0,
      "application_id": "north-application-2026-10-05",
      "provider_field_id": "north-field",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "attempts": 0,
      "error": null,
      "started_at": "2026-10-02T14:00:00.000Z",
      "completed_at": "2026-10-02T14:00:00.000Z",
      "result": {
        "success": true,
        "esa_required": false,
        "provider_id": "your-provider",
        "account_id": "your-account",
        "products": [{ "epa_number": "66222-36", "product_name": "Atrazine 4L", "pest": ["Waterhemp"], "product_status": "Active", "esa_required": false, "pulas": [] }],
        "summary": { "total_pulas": 0, "total_limitations": 0, "products_checked": 1, "products_with_limitations": 0 },
        "compliance": {
          "version": 1,
          "scope": "requirements_and_gaps",
          "calculated_at": "2026-10-02T14:00:00.000Z",
          "processing_complete": true,
          "status": "not_applicable",
          "runoff": [],
          "drift": { "status": "not_applicable", "requirements": null, "reductions": [] },
          "soil": { "status": "not_applicable" },
          "issues": []
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Idempotency and retention

The same key and effective input return the existing job with `replayed: true`. Changing inputs returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Without the header, each accepted submission creates a new job. Jobs and replay keys expire 30 days after completion; after expiration, the same key can create a new job.

Split larger submissions into jobs of at most 100 fields. They may share `provider_group_id`, but each job needs its own idempotency key. A full processing backlog returns `429 BULK_BACKLOG_EXCEEDED` for jobs that need queue processing. Confirmed no-ESA jobs can still complete immediately. Request rate limits apply to both paths.

```bash cURL
curl --request POST 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/esa-check/bulk' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Idempotency-Key: work-order-42-first-pass' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "provider_id": "your-provider",
  "account_id": "your-account",
  "provider_group_id": "work-order-42",
  "application_method": "Broadcast-Ground",
  "application_date": "2026-10-05",
  "products": [
    {
      "epa_number": "7969-500",
      "product_name": "Liberty Ultra",
      "rate": 32,
      "rate_unit": "fl oz/ac",
      "rate_unit_state": "L"
    }
  ],
  "crop": [
    "Corn"
  ],
  "pest": [
    "Waterhemp"
  ],
  "gpa": 15,
  "droplet_size": "VC",
  "boom_height": "low",
  "include_soil_analysis": true,
  "include_mitigations": true,
  "fields": [
    {
      "application_id": "north-application-2026-10-05",
      "provider_field_id": "north-field",
      "field_name": "North field",
      "field_boundary": {
        "type": "Feature",
        "properties": {},
        "geometry": {
          "type": "Polygon",
          "coordinates": [
            [
              [
                -95.404,
                43.102
              ],
              [
                -95.392,
                43.102
              ],
              [
                -95.392,
                43.11
              ],
              [
                -95.404,
                43.11
              ],
              [
                -95.404,
                43.102
              ]
            ]
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "application_id": "south-application-2026-10-05",
      "provider_field_id": "south-field",
      "field_name": "South field",
      "field_boundary": {
        "type": "Feature",
        "properties": {},
        "geometry": {
          "type": "Polygon",
          "coordinates": [
            [
              [
                -95.404,
                43.092
              ],
              [
                -95.392,
                43.092
              ],
              [
                -95.392,
                43.1
              ],
              [
                -95.404,
                43.1
              ],
              [
                -95.404,
                43.092
              ]
            ]
          ]
        }
      },
      "crop": [
        "Soybeans"
      ],
      "gpa": 20,
      "boom_height": null,
      "products": [
        {
          "epa_number": "7969-500",
          "product_name": "Liberty Ultra",
          "rate": 28,
          "rate_unit": "fl oz/ac",
          "rate_unit_state": "L"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}'
```

```json 202
{
  "success": true,
  "job_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "status": "queued",
  "total_items": 2,
  "replayed": false,
  "status_url": "/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "results_url": "/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001/results"
}
```

## Errors

Submission-specific errors are `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and `429 BULK_BACKLOG_EXCEEDED`. Invalid defaults, overrides, duplicate identities, group IDs, or idempotency headers return `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. No job is created for a validation error.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Get bulk job status

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/bulk-status.md

> Read processing progress and terminal counts

Endpoint: `GET https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/{job_id}`

Read processing progress and terminal counts.

### job_id

path parameter; string; required.

Opaque job identifier from the accepted response.

## Job lifecycle

`status` is `queued`, `processing`, `completed`, `completed_with_errors`, or `failed`. The last three are terminal. `completed` means every item succeeded, `completed_with_errors` means some items succeeded and some failed, and `failed` means no item succeeded.

A job whose products are all confirmed to have no ESA requirement starts as `completed` during submission. Its results are returned inline by the submission endpoint, so you do not need to poll it.

`counts` reports queued, processing, succeeded, and failed items. `started_at`, `completed_at`, and `expires_at` can be null while work is pending. Results expire 30 days after terminal completion.

Poll with backoff (for example, every five seconds). Responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`. A different provider or expired/unknown job receives `404 BULK_JOB_NOT_FOUND`.

```bash cURL
curl --request GET 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY"
```

```json 200
{
  "success": true,
  "job_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "provider_id": "your-provider",
  "account_id": "your-account",
  "provider_group_id": "work-order-42",
  "status": "queued",
  "total_items": 2,
  "counts": {
    "queued": 2,
    "processing": 0,
    "succeeded": 0,
    "failed": 0
  },
  "created_at": "2026-10-05T14:00:00.000Z",
  "started_at": null,
  "completed_at": null,
  "expires_at": null,
  "status_url": "/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "results_url": "/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001/results"
}
```

## Errors

A malformed job UUID returns `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. An unknown, expired, or other-provider job returns `404 BULK_JOB_NOT_FOUND`.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Get bulk results

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/bulk-results.md

> Read paginated results in original submission order

Endpoint: `GET https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/{job_id}/results`

Read paginated results in original submission order.

### job_id

path parameter; string; required.

Job identifier returned by submission.

### offset

query parameter; integer; optional; default: 0.

Zero-based offset, 0–100.

### limit

query parameter; integer; optional; default: 20.

Page size, 1–50.

## Item results

Jobs completed during the submission product check have succeeded items with `attempts: 0`. They never entered the processing queue. These results are also returned inline in the submission response and remain available here for the same retention period.

Items remain in submission order (`item_index` starts at zero). Each has `application_id`, `provider_field_id`, `status`, `attempts`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `result`, and `error`. New pending items have null result/error; queued items awaiting a retry may retain an error from an earlier attempt. Starting the next attempt clears that error. Treat `status` as authoritative. Succeeded items contain the same response structure as a single check. Failed items contain `{ code, message, retryable }` under `error`.

Read `result.compliance` for succeeded checks; item success does not imply compliance. Product PULA limitations are under `result.products[].pulas[].limitations`, with counts in `result.summary`; see [product PULA limitations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/esa-check#product-pula-limitations). Follow `next_offset` until it is null. You can read results before the job completes, but queued/processing items are not final. Save the results you need before the 30-day retention window ends. Responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The example below shows a processing job. The first item succeeded and its product has a PULA limitation; the second item is still queued. The succeeded `result` shows selected fields only.

```bash cURL
curl --request GET 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/esa-check/bulk/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001/results?offset=0&limit=20' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY"
```

```json 200
{
  "success": true,
  "job_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "total_items": 2,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 20,
  "next_offset": null,
  "items": [
    {
      "item_index": 0,
      "application_id": "north-application-2026-10-05",
      "provider_field_id": "north-field",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "attempts": 1,
      "error": null,
      "started_at": "2026-10-05T14:00:05.000Z",
      "completed_at": "2026-10-05T14:00:09.000Z",
      "result": {
        "success": true,
        "esa_required": true,
        "account_id": "your-account",
        "provider_id": "your-provider",
        "application_event_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002",
        "products": [
          {
            "epa_number": "7969-500",
            "product_name": "Liberty Ultra",
            "pest": ["Waterhemp"],
            "product_status": "Active",
            "esa_required": true,
            "pulas": [
              {
                "pula_id": 12345,
                "event_name": "Example PULA",
                "status": "effective",
                "effective_date": "2026-01-01",
                "codes": "EX1",
                "limitations": [
                  {
                    "limitation_id": 67890,
                    "code": "EX1",
                    "limitation": "Illustrative limitation text. Read the returned text for the actual restriction.",
                    "mitigation_options": []
                  }
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
        ],
        "summary": { "total_pulas": 1, "total_limitations": 1, "products_checked": 1, "products_with_limitations": 1 },
        "compliance": {
          "version": 1,
          "scope": "requirements_and_gaps",
          "calculated_at": "2026-10-05T14:00:09.000Z",
          "processing_complete": true,
          "status": "indeterminate",
          "issues": [
            { "code": "LIMITATIONS_REVIEW_REQUIRED", "message": "Review the returned PULA text for conditions not evaluated automatically" },
            { "code": "DRIFT_CONDITIONS_UNVERIFIED", "message": "Buffer placement and application weather have not been verified" }
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "item_index": 1,
      "application_id": "south-application-2026-10-05",
      "provider_field_id": "south-field",
      "status": "queued",
      "attempts": 0,
      "result": null,
      "error": null,
      "started_at": null,
      "completed_at": null
    }
  ]
}
```

## Errors

An invalid job UUID, offset, or limit returns `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. An unknown, expired, or other-provider job returns `404 BULK_JOB_NOT_FOUND`. HTTP 200 can contain failed items; see [bulk item failures and retry examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#bulk-item-failures).

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

## Runoff exemptions after processing

See [Understanding compliance determinations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/compliance-determination) for runoff and drift scoring, setup violations, overall status, and when to refresh a result.

Each successful item follows the [ESA check runoff rules](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/esa-check#runoff-requirements-and-portal-exemptions): EPA runoff is required by default, and a saved portal exemption satisfies that application's EPA runoff obligation. Completed item results are processing-time snapshots. To read later portal edits, use [application compliance](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/application-compliance) or [group compliance](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/group-compliance).

# V2: Analyze soil

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/soil-process.md

> Analyze hydrologic soil groups and slope for a field boundary

Endpoint: `POST https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/soil/process`

Analyze hydrologic soil groups and slope for a field boundary.

### provider_id

body parameter; string; required.

Your assigned provider identifier, matching the API key.

### field_boundary

body parameter; object; required.

GeoJSON Feature with Polygon or MultiPolygon in EPSG:4326. The single-check field-boundary limits apply.

## Response

The response contains `soil_data` (a GeoJSON FeatureCollection clipped to the field boundary), `dominant_hydgrpdcd`, `total_area_sqm`, `hydgrpdcd_analysis`, `weighted_avg_slopegradwta`, and `musym_analysis`. Missing hydrologic group or slope attributes can be null.

This endpoint does not save a field/application. Soil may be reused across requests for the same area. The example shows summary fields; the complete response also includes field-boundary data and map-unit analysis.

```bash cURL
curl --request POST 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/soil/process' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "provider_id": "your-provider",
  "field_boundary": {
    "type": "Feature",
    "properties": {},
    "geometry": {
      "type": "Polygon",
      "coordinates": [
        [
          [
            -95.404,
            43.102
          ],
          [
            -95.392,
            43.102
          ],
          [
            -95.392,
            43.11
          ],
          [
            -95.404,
            43.11
          ],
          [
            -95.404,
            43.102
          ]
        ]
      ]
    }
  }
}'
```

```json 200 — selected response fields
{
  "dominant_hydgrpdcd": "B",
  "total_area_sqm": 865700.0,
  "hydgrpdcd_analysis": {
    "B": {
      "area_sqm": 865700.0,
      "percentage": 100
    }
  },
  "weighted_avg_slopegradwta": 2.1
}
```

## Errors

Invalid field boundaries return `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. A dependency failure can return `503 REQUEST_FAILED`; capacity and deadline errors also apply.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Runoff baseline

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/runoff-baseline.md

> Calculate automatic runoff mitigation credits without saving a field

Endpoint: `POST https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/field/runoff-baseline`

Calculate automatic runoff mitigation credits without saving a field.

### field_boundary

body parameter; object; required.

A GeoJSON Feature or bare Polygon/MultiPolygon in EPSG:4326. A FeatureCollection with exactly one field is also accepted. A JSON string containing one supported value is accepted.

## Response

`baseline_points` is the sum of `auto_credits`. Each credit includes `sub_option_id`, `label`, `points`, and `source` (`always`, `slope`, `soil`, or `county`). The response also includes `counties`, a `soil_data` summary, `processing_complete`, and `issues`.

These are available automatic credits, not a product-specific compliance determination. The endpoint does not save a field/application. If soil is unavailable, it returns a partial baseline with `processing_complete: false` and `SOIL_UNAVAILABLE`; do not treat that partial sum as the full baseline.

The example shows selected response fields when soil could not be processed. Available non-soil credits are still returned.

```bash cURL
curl --request POST 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/field/runoff-baseline' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "field_boundary": {
    "type": "Feature",
    "properties": {},
    "geometry": {
      "type": "Polygon",
      "coordinates": [
        [
          [
            -95.404,
            43.102
          ],
          [
            -95.392,
            43.102
          ],
          [
            -95.392,
            43.11
          ],
          [
            -95.404,
            43.11
          ],
          [
            -95.404,
            43.102
          ]
        ]
      ]
    }
  }
}'
```

```json 200 — selected response fields
{
  "soil_data": null,
  "processing_complete": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "code": "SOIL_UNAVAILABLE",
      "message": "Baseline excludes soil-dependent credits; retry for a complete result"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Errors

Invalid field boundaries return `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. Missing soil can instead return HTTP 200 with `processing_complete: false` and the `SOIL_UNAVAILABLE` issue. Inspect completeness before using the baseline.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Process a field

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/process-field.md

> Save a field with soil analysis and automatic runoff credits

Endpoint: `POST https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/process-field`

Save a field with soil analysis and automatic runoff credits.

## Request

### provider_id

body parameter; string; required.

Your assigned provider identifier.

### account_id

body parameter; string; required.

Your account identifier.

### provider_field_id

body parameter; string; required.

Required external field identifier.

### field_name

body parameter; string; required.

Field name displayed in the portal and compliance reports.

### field_boundary

body parameter; object; required.

GeoJSON Feature with Polygon/MultiPolygon in EPSG:4326; uses single-check boundary validation.

### year

body parameter; integer; optional.

Year for automatic runoff credits, 1900–2200; defaults to the current UTC year.

### include_mitigation_options

body parameter; boolean; optional; default: false.

Include the EPA runoff option tree with selected measures.

## Processing behavior

This endpoint saves a field, its processed soil, and automatic annual runoff credits. It does not create an application or run a product-specific assessment. Soil must complete before this update is saved; soil failure leaves the existing field data intact.

## Response

The response includes your `provider_field_id`, `year`, portal link fields, `soil_data`, `counties`, `pulas`, `mitigations_applied`, `steps`, and `summary`. `mitigation_options` is null unless requested. `steps.soil.data.status` distinguishes `reused` from `fetched`; `fetched` can still reuse soil source data for the area.

The example shows selected fields only.

```bash cURL
curl --request POST 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/process-field' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "provider_id": "your-provider",
  "account_id": "your-account",
  "provider_field_id": "north-field",
  "field_name": "North field",
  "field_boundary": {
    "type": "Feature",
    "properties": {},
    "geometry": {
      "type": "Polygon",
      "coordinates": [
        [
          [
            -95.404,
            43.102
          ],
          [
            -95.392,
            43.102
          ],
          [
            -95.392,
            43.11
          ],
          [
            -95.404,
            43.11
          ],
          [
            -95.404,
            43.102
          ]
        ]
      ]
    }
  },
  "year": 2026,
  "include_mitigation_options": true
}'
```

```json 200 — selected response fields
{
  "success": true,
  "provider_field_id": "north-field",
  "year": 2026,
  "steps": {
    "spatial": {
      "success": true
    },
    "soil": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "status": "reused"
      }
    },
    "mitigations": {
      "success": true
    }
  },
  "summary": {
    "pula_count": 0,
    "soil_available": true,
    "mitigations_applied_count": 2,
    "total_points": 3
  }
}
```

## Errors

Field processing can return `409 DUPLICATE_FIELD`, `FIELD_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT`, `PROCESSING_CONFLICT`, or `FIELD_CHANGED`, and `503 PORTAL_SAS_UNCONFIGURED` when signed portal links are unavailable.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Get runoff mitigation options

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/mitigations.md

> Read the active EPA runoff mitigation option tree

Endpoint: `GET https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/mitigations/{mitigation_type}`

Read the active EPA runoff mitigation option tree.

### mitigation_type

path parameter; string; required.

Only `epa_runoff` is supported. Other values return 422.

## Response

`categories` contains active categories in display order. Each category has `options`; each option has `sub_options`. Options contain labels and available runoff points. Use the returned identifiers and definitions when presenting choices, rather than hardcoding a points catalog.

A valid type with no active definitions returns an empty categories array. The example shows that empty-catalog response.

```bash cURL
curl --request GET 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/mitigations/epa_runoff' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY"
```

```json 200
{
  "mitigation_type": "epa_runoff",
  "categories": []
}
```

## Errors

A mitigation type other than `epa_runoff` returns `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. Dependency and capacity errors can also apply.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Get application compliance

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/application-compliance.md

> Retrieve saved requirements, current runoff credits, and full drift configuration for an application

Endpoint: `GET https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/{application_event_id}/compliance`

Read compliance information after an ESA check or after an applicator changes selections in the portal. The response combines saved application requirements with current mitigation selections. Every request reads fresh data and returns `Cache-Control: no-store`.

### application_event_id

path parameter; string; required.

Application-event reference returned by an ESA check. Use this UUID, not your submitted `application_id`.

### include_geometry

query parameter; boolean; optional; default: false.

Use `true` to include saved `buffer_features` and any PULA boundaries included in the last assessment. Only literal `true` and `false` are accepted. This does not compute new buffer or treatable-area boundaries.

## Response fields

The response contains `success`, `retrieved_at`, and `application`. Group retrieval returns this same application object for each member.

| Field under `application` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `application_event_id`, `application_id` | API application reference and your submitted application identifier. |
| `account_id`, `provider_group_id`, `provider_field_id`, `field_name` | Account, group, and field context. Optional identifiers can be null. |
| `application_date`, `application_method`, `products`, `crop`, `pest` | Current saved application inputs. |
| `processing_status`, `updated_at`, `portal_locked_at` | Application processing state, last application update, and portal lock timestamp. Child selections can change independently of `updated_at`. |
| `compliance.scope` | Always `saved_requirements_and_current_selections`. |
| `compliance.requirements[]` | Every saved mitigation requirement, including `mitigation_type`, effective `required`, nullable `required_points`, `updated_at`, runoff exemption selections (plus `exempt` and `label_required_points` for EPA runoff), and any requirement-specific `drift_buffers`. |
| `compliance.runoff[]` | Current runoff scoring for each saved runoff requirement. EPA runoff and Enlist remain separate. |
| `compliance.drift` | Full saved drift configuration, current reductions and selections, setup, weather, and historical computation details. |
| `compliance.last_assessment` | Last saved ESA assessment: `calculated_at`, `status`, `processing_complete`, `issues`, and `products[]` with their PULA limitations. Null when no assessment was saved. |

### Product PULA limitations

`compliance.last_assessment.products[]` returns each product's saved `epa_number`, `product_name`, `pest`, `product_status`, `esa_required`, and `pulas[]`. Each PULA has `pula_id`, `event_name`, `status`, `effective_date`, `codes`, and `limitations[]` with `limitation_id`, `code`, `limitation` text, and `mitigation_options`. With `include_geometry=true`, a PULA also includes its saved `geometry` when the original check requested it. These fields match the [ESA check product limitations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/esa-check#product-pula-limitations).

Limitations come from the last ESA check; this GET does not search for new or changed PULAs. Resubmit the check to refresh them. An application without a saved assessment has `last_assessment: null`.

## Runoff points and applicability

See [Understanding compliance determinations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/compliance-determination) for runoff and drift scoring, setup violations, overall status, and when to refresh a result.

Each runoff entry includes `mitigation_type`, `year`, `required`, `exempt`, `required_points`, `label_required_points`, `earned_points`, `gap`, `status`, `credited_measures`, `selected_measures`, exemption claims, and `issues`.

- `required_points` is the effective requirement: zero for an accepted EPA runoff exemption, otherwise the saved target. `label_required_points` retains the saved label/PULA target, including for exempt applications. Null means unresolved; it does not mean zero.
- `earned_points` is recalculated from current selections using active definitions, product restrictions, soil eligibility, selection limits, and aggregation caps. `credited_measures` explains the credits counted. `selected_measures` also includes selections that did not qualify for credit, with source, implementation date, and notes.
- `gap` is the larger of zero and required minus earned points. It is null when required points are unresolved.
- `year` comes from `application_date`. Applications on the same field in the same year share runoff selections, but their product restrictions and required points can differ.
- `status` is `met`, `not_met`, or `indeterminate` for runoff within this scope. For non-exempt requirements, a missing soil result, unknown product, incomplete application processing, unresolved requirement, unsupported mitigation type, or unverified non-EPA applicability keeps it `indeterminate`. An accepted EPA exemption returns `met` without requiring runoff scoring inputs.

Runoff `issues` contains code strings: `RUNOFF_APPLICABILITY_UNVERIFIED`, `RUNOFF_REQUIREMENT_UNRESOLVED`, `SOIL_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNKNOWN_PRODUCT`, `APPLICATION_PROCESSING_INCOMPLETE`, or `UNSUPPORTED_MITIGATION`.

EPA runoff is required by default, including older unanswered records saved with `required: false`. An explicit portal exemption (`required: false` with an evaluation timestamp) returns `required: false`, `exempt: true`, `status: "met"`, `required_points: 0`, and `gap: 0`. `runoff_exemption_claimed_at` and `runoff_exemption_reasons` preserve the selection; timestamped legacy exemptions without reason codes are supported. Choosing “None apply” restores `required: true` and scoring against the saved target. The `requirements[]` and `runoff[]` entries use the same effective requirement.

Portal selections appear on the next GET without resubmitting a check. EPA exemptions do not exempt Enlist, other runoff systems, or drift. `RUNOFF_APPLICABILITY_UNVERIFIED` is no longer emitted for EPA runoff; it can still describe an optional non-EPA runoff requirement. Historical `last_assessment` values and completed bulk results are unchanged until a new check is run.

## Drift configuration and details

`compliance.drift.configuration` returns the complete saved configuration, or null when none exists. Inspect its `version`; current V2 checks produce version 4 with:

- `computed_at` and `summary` for `wind_directional`, `omni_directional`, and `downslope` buffers. Summaries separate `mitigatable` and `non_mitigatable` distances.
- `requirements[]` with source (`product` or `pula_limitation`), `product_epa`, `config_label`, `limitation_id` when available, matched method, and `raw_distance_ft`.
- Complete `buffers_esa` for each requirement, including anchor, exclusion categories, mitigation eligibility, methods, distance units, droplet/boom tiers, wind-speed ranges, rate ranges, and mitigation types when configured.
- Raw and normalized rates, rate resolution, active-ingredient information, and flags indicating conditional wind/rate tiers when available.

`reductions[]` returns current saved totals and selected mitigations by drift type. Each selection includes its label, definition points and reduction percentage, custom value, and implementation notes. These totals are recorded selections; they are not newly verified buffer reductions.

`setup` includes normalized application method, GPA, droplet size, and boom height. `weather` includes wind direction, wind speed, temperature, humidity, observation timestamp, and source. Wind direction is where wind comes **from**, clockwise from north; speed is mph, temperature is °F, and humidity is percent. `adjuvant_results` contains the saved adjuvant evaluation, or null.

`last_computation` contains the last application-time computation's timestamp, overall `status`, separate `drift_status`, inputs, reductions, manual claims, feature counts/scope, per-edge details, and product breakdown, or null. It can predate current selections or weather. `drift_status: "met"` means the supplied setup satisfied the configured drift rules when applied within the calculated treatable area, even if a buffer remained. This is a saved result, not a fresh drift assessment. Older computations have a null `drift_status` until recomputed. With `include_geometry=true`, `buffer_features` contains saved portal features, or null; it is separate from that historical computation.

## Fresh reads and saved assessments

This GET request does not rerun an ESA check, fetch new soil, refresh product/PULA requirements, or recompute drift placement. There is no new overall `compliance.status`; read current runoff status separately from `last_assessment.status`. A current runoff `met` result does not establish overall application compliance. Missing assessment/configuration data remains null or empty, including while processing is pending or failed.

To refresh the saved requirements, resubmit the application to [ESA check](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/esa-check). To calculate buffers using application-time weather and receive buffer/treatable-area boundaries, use [compute drift buffers](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/drift-buffer). No-ESA checks that did not create an application-event reference cannot be retrieved here. An expired or locked portal does not prevent an authorized provider from reading an existing application; archived fields are excluded.

```bash cURL
curl --request GET 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002/compliance?include_geometry=false' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY"
```

```json 200
{
  "success": true,
  "retrieved_at": "2026-10-02T14:00:00.000Z",
  "application": {
    "application_event_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002",
    "application_id": "north-application-2026-10-05",
    "account_id": "your-account",
    "provider_group_id": "work-order-42",
    "provider_field_id": "north-field",
    "field_name": "North field",
    "application_date": "2026-10-05",
    "application_method": "Broadcast-Ground",
    "products": [{ "epa_number": "123-456", "product_name": "Example product", "rate": 16, "rate_unit": "fl oz/acre", "pest": ["weeds"] }],
    "crop": ["corn"],
    "pest": ["weeds"],
    "processing_status": "completed",
    "updated_at": "2026-10-02T13:00:00.000Z",
    "portal_locked_at": null,
    "compliance": {
      "scope": "saved_requirements_and_current_selections",
      "requirements": [
        {
          "mitigation_type": "epa_runoff",

```

The example uses illustrative product requirements. Use your returned configuration and labels for the actual application.

## Errors

An absent or other-provider application, or one on an archived field, returns `404 APPLICATION_NOT_FOUND`. A malformed application UUID, invalid query value, or unknown query parameter returns `422 INVALID_REQUEST`.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Get group compliance

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/group-compliance.md

> Retrieve paginated compliance information for an account-scoped application group

Endpoint: `GET https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/groups/{provider_group_id}/compliance`

Read saved requirements, current runoff points, and full drift configuration for applications in a group. Provider identity comes from your API key. You must also supply `account_id` because group identifiers can repeat across accounts.

### provider_group_id

path parameter; string; required.

Your job or work-order identifier, up to 200 characters. URL-encode the value.

### account_id

query parameter; string; required.

Account identifier supplied when creating the applications, up to 200 characters.

### offset

query parameter; integer; optional; default: 0.

Zero-based offset, from 0 to 1,000,000. Use the returned `next_offset` for the next page.

### limit

query parameter; integer; optional; default: 50.

Page size, from 1 to 100 applications.

### include_geometry

query parameter; boolean; optional; default: false.

Include saved buffer features and any saved PULA boundaries for each application. Accepts literal `true` or `false`. No new geometry is computed.

## Group scope and pagination

See [Understanding compliance determinations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/compliance-determination) for runoff and drift scoring, setup violations, overall status, and when to refresh a result.

`applications[]` contains the same complete application objects returned by [get application compliance](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/application-compliance), including requirements, runoff scoring and claims, full drift configuration, current reductions, setup/weather, and the last saved assessment with each product's [PULA limitations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/application-compliance#product-pula-limitations) under `compliance.last_assessment.products[].pulas[].limitations`. That page defines every nested field and how to interpret current selections versus historical assessments.

The response also includes `retrieved_at`, `account_id`, `provider_group_id`, `total`, `offset`, `limit`, and `next_offset`. `total` counts existing accessible applications in this group and account. Members are ordered by application-event reference. Continue until `next_offset` is null. An offset beyond the last member returns an empty array with the total preserved. An empty or unowned group returns 404.

Each page reads one consistent database snapshot. Separate pages can reflect later changes. Wait for [bulk completion](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/bulk-status) before retrieving a complete job; pending bulk items may not have an application yet. If group membership changes while paging, start again at offset zero.

EPA runoff is required by default. Each application’s saved portal exemption returns runoff `status: "met"`, `required: false`, `exempt: true`, and zero effective required points. Portal edits are reflected on the next GET; historical assessments remain separate. See [runoff applicability](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/application-compliance#runoff-points-and-applicability) for details.

There is no group-wide compliance verdict or sum of runoff points. Applications on the same field/year share selections, so adding their points would double-count credits. Inspect each application's runoff results and last assessment separately. A successful retrieval does not mean the applications are compliant.

Requests are read-only and return `Cache-Control: no-store`. Portal locks or expiry do not block these provider reads; archived fields are excluded. Reading this endpoint does not refresh the saved requirements or compute drift placement.

```bash cURL
curl --get 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/groups/work-order-42/compliance' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode 'account_id=your-account' \
  --data-urlencode 'offset=0' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=50' \
  --data-urlencode 'include_geometry=false'
```

This response shows two applications. The first has a saved assessment with a product PULA limitation under `last_assessment.products`. Its drift details are trimmed; see [application compliance](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/application-compliance) for the complete object. The second is still waiting for processing. Empty requirement lists and null assessments do not establish that no mitigations are needed.

```json 200
{
  "success": true,
  "retrieved_at": "2026-10-02T14:00:00.000Z",
  "account_id": "your-account",
  "provider_group_id": "work-order-42",
  "total": 2,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 50,
  "next_offset": null,
  "applications": [
    {
      "application_event_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002",
```

## Errors

No accessible applications for the group/account returns `404 GROUP_NOT_FOUND`. A missing account, malformed pagination, invalid geometry flag, or unknown query parameter returns `422 INVALID_REQUEST`. Arrays and repeated query values are not accepted.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Enlist compliance report

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/enlist-report.md

> Download the Enlist compliance report for a provider-owned field

Endpoint: `GET https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/fields/{provider_field_id}/reports/enlist`

Download the Enlist compliance report for a provider-owned field.

### provider_field_id

path parameter; string; required.

Your field identifier from the single check, bulk field entry, or field-processing request.

### year

query parameter; integer; optional.

Optional report year, 1900–2200.

## Response

A successful request returns **200** with `Content-Type: application/pdf` and an attachment filename. Save the response bytes as a `.pdf` file.

```http 200
Content-Type: application/pdf
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=mitigation-report.pdf
```

The field must belong to your provider and have an active, unexpired, unarchived portal. An unknown or unavailable field returns 404; an ambiguous field identifier returns 409. Dependent report failures can return 502. The report uses the field's current saved data; the download request does not rerun the ESA check.

The example requests the 2026 report.

```bash cURL
curl --request GET 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/fields/north-field/reports/enlist?year=2026' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --output enlist-report.pdf
```

## Errors

Report errors are `404 FIELD_NOT_FOUND`, `409 DUPLICATE_FIELD`, `502 INVALID_REPORT`, `503 PORTAL_SERVICE_UNCONFIGURED` or `PORTAL_SAS_UNCONFIGURED`, and `PORTAL_REQUEST_FAILED` with HTTP 400, 403, 404, 422, or 502. Error bodies use JSON even though successful responses are PDFs.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

---

```http 200
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=mitigation-report.pdf
```

The field must belong to your provider and have an active, unexpired, unarchived portal. An unknown or unavailable field returns 404; an ambiguous field identifier returns 409. All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

# V2: Issue portal access

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/portal-access.md

> Issue an expiring portal link for one application

Endpoint: `POST https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/{application_event_id}/portal-access`

Issue an expiring portal link for one application.

## Request

### application_event_id

path parameter; string; required.

Opaque application-event reference returned by an ESA check.

### ttl_seconds

body parameter; integer; optional.

Link lifetime, 60–86,400 seconds. Defaults to your configured lifetime (one hour by default).

### return_url

body parameter; string; optional.

Optional absolute HTTP(S) URL used to return the user when this link is rejected as expired; maximum 2,000 characters.

## Response and access

Returns an expiring `portal_url`, `expires_at`, `application_event_id`, `provider_group_id`, and the provider's `portal_access_mode`. Treat the URL as an opaque credential and use it unchanged. Do not derive or parse its token format.

This endpoint issues a signed expiring link in either access mode. In signed-link mode, the normal ESA-check response already provides an expiring `mitigation_portal_url`; an extra call is often unnecessary. In token mode, this endpoint lets you issue a short-lived link without changing your provider's default access mode.

The application must belong to your provider and its portal must be available. A grouped application link also supports navigation between applications in its job group. A portal lock prevents mitigation writes but does not prevent reading the portal.

The example shows selected response fields. Its placeholder URL represents the complete URL returned by the service.

```bash cURL
curl --request POST 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002/portal-access' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "return_url": "https://partner.example/applications/north"
}'
```

```json 200 — selected response fields
{
  "success": true,
  "application_event_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002",
  "provider_group_id": "work-order-42",
  "portal_url": "https://acreblitz.com/esaportal/field?t=opaque-returned-credential",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-05T15:00:00.000Z",
  "portal_access_mode": "token"
}
```

## Errors

Endpoint-specific errors are `404 APPLICATION_NOT_FOUND`, `403 INVALID_TOKEN`, `INACTIVE_TOKEN`, or `PORTAL_EXPIRED`, and `503 PORTAL_SAS_UNCONFIGURED`. Portal access denials refer to the field’s availability, not your API key.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

---

# V2: Set application portal lock

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/portal-lock.md

> Lock or unlock portal mitigation changes for one application

Endpoint: `PUT https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/{application_event_id}/portal-lock`

Lock or unlock portal mitigation changes for one application.

### application_event_id

path parameter; string; required.

Application-event reference returned by the check.

### locked

body parameter; boolean; required.

Use true to lock mitigation changes or false to unlock them.

## Lock behavior

The lock covers this application's mitigation writes and its shared field-year runoff selections. Reads and compliance report downloads remain available. Repeating a lock preserves the original `portal_locked_at` timestamp; unlocking returns null for that timestamp.

Applications sharing the same field/year share runoff selections. A lock on a sibling application can therefore keep those shared runoff writes locked even after this application is unlocked.

```bash cURL
curl --request PUT 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002/portal-lock' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "locked": true
}'
```

```json 200
{
  "success": true,
  "application_event_id": "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002",
  "locked": true,
  "portal_locked_at": "2026-10-05T14:05:00.000Z"
}
```

## Errors

An absent or other-provider application returns `404 APPLICATION_NOT_FOUND`. A missing/non-boolean `locked` value or malformed application UUID returns `422 INVALID_REQUEST`.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

---

# V2: Set group portal lock

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/group-portal-lock.md

> Lock or unlock all current applications in an account-scoped group

Endpoint: `PUT https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/groups/{provider_group_id}/portal-lock`

Lock or unlock all current applications in an account-scoped group.

### provider_group_id

path parameter; string; required.

Your job/work-order identifier, up to 200 characters.

### account_id

body parameter; string; required.

Required account identifier. Group identifiers may repeat across accounts.

### locked

body parameter; boolean; required.

Use true to lock current applications or false to unlock them.

## Group scope

The operation applies to existing applications owned by your provider with this account and group. It returns their application-event references. An empty or unowned group returns 404.

New applications added afterward start unlocked. Wait for bulk completion before locking a complete job, and call again after adding applications. Group unlock also clears locks set individually on those applications. Shared runoff selections follow the same field/year lock rule as an individual application lock.

```bash cURL
curl --request PUT 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/groups/work-order-42/portal-lock' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "account_id": "your-account",
  "locked": true
}'
```

```json 200
{
  "success": true,
  "provider_group_id": "work-order-42",
  "account_id": "your-account",
  "locked": true,
  "application_event_ids": [
    "019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002"
  ]
}
```

## Errors

No applications for the supplied group/account returns `404 GROUP_NOT_FOUND`. Invalid or missing account, group, or lock values return `422 INVALID_REQUEST`.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.

---

# V2: Compute application-time drift buffers

Source: https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/drift-buffer.md

> Refresh an application assessment with current wind and application setup

Endpoint: `POST https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/{application_event_id}/drift-buffer/compute`

Refresh an application assessment with current wind and application setup.

## Request

### application_event_id

path parameter; string; required.

Opaque application-event reference from a previous ESA check.

### wind_direction_deg

body parameter; number; required.

Wind direction in degrees, greater than or equal to 0 and less than 360.

### wind_speed_mph

body parameter; number; required.

Wind speed, 0–80 mph.

### temperature_f

body parameter; number; optional.

Optional observed temperature, -100–200 degrees Fahrenheit; nullable.

### humidity_percent

body parameter; number; optional.

Optional observed humidity, 0–100; nullable.

### application_method

body parameter; string; optional.

Optional supported method; otherwise use the saved method.

### droplet_size

body parameter; string; optional.

Optional supported category/code; nullable. An omitted value uses the saved value; explicit null clears it.

### boom_height

body parameter; string; optional.

Optional `low` or `high`; nullable. An omitted value uses the saved value; explicit null clears it.

### gpa

body parameter; number; optional.

Optional positive spray gallons per acre; nullable. An omitted value uses the saved value; explicit null clears it.

### rate_updates

body parameter; object[]; optional.

Up to 100 rate changes. Each requires `product_index` (zero-based), `epa_number`, nonnegative `rate`, and nonempty `rate_unit`; optional `rate_unit_state` and positive `row_spacing_inches`. The index and registration must match the saved product.

### geometry

body parameter; string; optional.

`none`, `buffer`, `treatable`, or `both`; defaults to `none`.

## Assessment behavior

See [Understanding compliance determinations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/compliance-determination) for runoff and drift scoring, setup violations, overall status, and when to refresh a result.

The endpoint resolves your saved application, applies current weather/setup inputs and rate changes, and returns a refreshed check plus `application_time`. Weather and the assessment are saved for that application. It checks the application revision; conflicting changes return 409.

`application_time` includes submitted inputs, effective rates, reductions, manual mitigation claims, feature scope, feature counts, per-edge buffers, and product-specific buffer details. Requested field-boundary output is returned under `application_time.geometry` and is not retained in the saved assessment snapshot.

Read `compliance.drift.status` for drift and `compliance.status` for the overall application assessment. `application_time.drift_status` repeats the drift result; `application_time.status` repeats the overall result. Runoff shortfalls and unresolved PULA restrictions can prevent an overall pass even when drift is `met`.

| Drift status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `met` | The supplied setup satisfies the configured drift rules and a treatable area has been calculated. Spray only within that area. A remaining buffer is a restriction to follow, not a failure. |
| `not_met` | A known setup violation exists, such as droplets below the label minimum, a high boom where the rule requires low, a disallowed mitigation selection, or no treatable area remaining. Correct the setup and recompute. |
| `indeterminate` | Required inputs or rules cannot be resolved, or a manual drift practice remains unverified. Read the issue codes. |
| `not_applicable` | No drift requirement applies. |

For an application-time assessment, `compliance.drift.scope` is `application_setup_and_treatable_area`. `requires_buffer` and `has_treatable_area` describe the calculated result; both are null when setup or rule resolution prevents calculation. A `met` result can have `requires_buffer: true`. It assesses your submitted setup and the calculated area; it does not certify where spraying actually occurred.

Use `geometry: "both"` to receive the buffer and treatable area together. `geometry: "none"` only omits the field-boundary output; it still performs the calculation and returns the same status. If setup is invalid or required rules are unresolved, requested output conservatively marks the entire field as buffer with `treatable: null`. When the calculated buffer consumes the whole field, drift returns `not_met` with `NO_TREATABLE_AREA`.

A successful calculation clears the generic `DRIFT_CONDITIONS_UNVERIFIED` issue. Specific issues remain: unknown products, missing required droplet/boom inputs, unresolved rate/wind tiers, unsupported omni-directional or downslope placement, and unverified manual practices prevent a drift pass. Rate-specific wind tiers take precedence over method-level tiers. Wind outside configured tiers returns `WIND_SPEED_UNRESOLVED`; the API does not infer an unconfigured wind limit. Temperature and humidity are recorded inputs, not currently evaluated label thresholds.

Protected features are read for each request so new nearby features can affect the result. Recompute after changing application conditions or mitigation selections. [Application compliance](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/application-compliance) and [group compliance](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/group-compliance) expose the saved `drift.last_computation.drift_status`; those GETs do not run a new placement calculation. Older snapshots have a null `drift_status` until recomputed.

The response also includes the refreshed `products[]` with each product's [PULA limitations](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/api-reference/endpoint/esa-check#product-pula-limitations) and the `summary` counts, in the same shape as an ESA check. Any matching limitation adds `LIMITATIONS_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, which keeps the overall `status` `indeterminate` even when drift is `met`.

The example shows selected response fields for an application with a remaining buffer, a treatable area, satisfied runoff, and no PULA limitations or other unresolved restrictions.

```bash cURL
curl --request POST 'https://esa.acreblitz.com/api/v2/applications/019953f8-8c00-7000-8000-000000000002/drift-buffer/compute' \
  --header "X-API-Key: $ACREBLITZ_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "wind_direction_deg": 180,
  "wind_speed_mph": 8,
  "temperature_f": 72,
  "humidity_percent": 55,
  "application_method": "Broadcast-Ground",
  "droplet_size": "VC",
  "boom_height": "low",
  "gpa": 15,
  "rate_updates": [
    {
      "product_index": 0,
      "epa_number": "7969-500",
      "rate": 28,
      "rate_unit": "fl oz/ac",
      "rate_unit_state": "L"
    }
  ],
  "geometry": "both"
}'
```


## Errors

Endpoint-specific errors include `404 APPLICATION_NOT_FOUND`; `422 NO_FIELD_GEOMETRY`, `PRODUCT_MISMATCH`, `INVALID_APPLICATION`, or `UNSUPPORTED_APPLICATION_METHOD`; and `409 DUPLICATE_FIELD`, `FIELD_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT`, `DUPLICATE_APPLICATION`, `APPLICATION_FIELD_CONFLICT`, `PROCESSING_CONFLICT`, `FIELD_CHANGED`, or `APPLICATION_CHANGED`. Signed portal setup can return `503 PORTAL_SAS_UNCONFIGURED`. See [assessment issues](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#assessment-issue-codes) for unresolved conditions returned with HTTP 200.

All routes can also return [authentication, validation, rate-limit, and dependency errors](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors#http-error-catalog). Use the [error catalog and examples](https://docs.acreblitz.com/v2/errors) to choose a retry or correction. Keep `X-Request-ID` when present.
